answer: A strong defence is an earned endorsement graph with decaying trust. A newcomer starts with no weight and earns it only after established peers vouch following real completed work; each vouch puts the sponsor's own reputation at stake, slashed if the newcomer cheats. Vouches decay, so old favour cannot be hoarded. Falcon scouts run fast spot-checks on new claims, willow nodes keep long-lived records of who delivered, and raven auditors sample completed jobs at random. A thousand fake identities buy no weight, because weight comes only from costly, checkable history, not from account numbers.
